items.teaser: For the first time since 1877, no male player with a one-handed backhand has reached a Grand Slam semi-final this season, marking the dec…
items.story:
For the first time since 1877, no male player with a one-handed backhand has reached a Grand Slam semi-final this season, marking the decline of a storied tennis tradition. Once dominant, the one-hander has given way to the more practical two-handed backhand. Modern coaching trends and the evolving speed of the game have contributed to its fading presence among top players.

items.headline: Indian bonds end flat as traders gauge RBI liquidity approach
items.teaser: In a cautious trading session, Indian government bonds experienced little movement as the Reserve Bank of India implemented temporary liq…
items.story: In a cautious trading session, Indian government bonds experienced little movement as the Reserve Bank of India implemented temporary liquidity management strategies. By withdrawing substantial amounts through variable rate reverse repos, the central bank aimed to counterbalance the influx from sizeable diaspora deposits. Additionally, the pressure from rising oil prices kept bond prices from gaining traction, although overnight indexed swap rates registered slight decreases throughout the day.

items.story: എൽപിജി സിലിണ്ടർ ബുക്ക് ചെയ്യാൻ 25 ദിവസം സമയപരിധി; നിയന്ത്രണം നീക്കി കേന്ദ്ര സർക്കാർ Manorama Onlineഅടുക്കളകൾക്ക് ആശ്വാസം; പാചകവാതക സിലിണ്ടർ ബുക്ക് ചെയ്യാനുള്ള നിയന്ത്രണത്തിൽ ഇളവ് വരുത്തി കേന്ദ്രം Mathrubhumiപാചകവാതക വിതരണത്തിൽ ആശ്വാസം; കേന്ദ്രം പുതിയ മാറ്റം വരുത്തിയതായി കേന്ദ്രമന്ത്രി സുരേഷ് ഗോപി Kerala Kaumudiഗാർഹിക എൽ.പി.ജി ഉപഭോക്താക്കൾക്ക് കേന്ദ്ര സമ്മാനം; ഇന്ത്യയിലെങ്ങും റീഫിൽ ബുക്കിങ് ഇടവേള ഇനി 25 ദിവസം The Economic Times Malayalamഎൽപിജി സിലിണ്ടർ ബുക്കിങ്: നിയന്ത്രണങ്ങളിൽ ഇളവ് വരുത്തി കേന്ദ

items.story: മന്ത്രിയുടെ ശബരിമല ക്യാമ്പിലേക്ക് ദേവസ്വം ബോർഡ് അറിയാതെ രണ്ട് നിയമനം; കടുത്ത അതൃപ്തിയിൽ ബോർഡ് Mathrubhumi‘മന്ത്രിയുമായി അഭിപ്രായ ഭിന്നതയില്ല; രാജിവയ്ക്കേണ്ട സാഹചര്യവുമില്ല: കാലാവധി പൂർത്തിയാക്കും’ Manorama Onlineശബരിമലയിൽ ഓണത്തിന് ഒരേ പന്തിയിൽ രണ്ട് വിളമ്പ് നടത്തി ; ദേവസ്വം ബോർഡിനെതിരെ ദേവസ്വം മന്ത്രി News18 Malayalam‘രാജിവെക്കില്ല; 2027 വരെ ദേവസ്വം ബോർഡ് പ്രസിഡന്റ് സ്ഥാനത്ത് തുടരും’ പ്രചരിക്കുന്ന വാർത്തകൾക്ക് അടിസ്ഥാനമില്ലെന്ന് കെ ജയകുമാർ SouthLive'രാജിവയ്ക്കാൻ ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്നില്ല'; സർക്കാരുമായി

items.headline: Park rangers and residents speak up to save Togo's last national park
items.teaser: A few years ago, I drove with an old friend from Togo, West Africa, towards the country's last remaining large protected area, Fazao-Malf…
items.story: A few years ago, I drove with an old friend from Togo, West Africa, towards the country's last remaining large protected area, Fazao-Malfakassa National Park. Our destination was the Hotel Fazao, where his uncle had once worked as a professional chef after its opening in 1980. For decades, while the park was managed by the Swiss Franz Weber Foundation (FWF), the hotel had hosted tourists from around the world who came to see elephants, monkeys, and other wildlife for which Africa is famous.

items.story: Researchers at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin (KUL) and the University of Eastern Finland have developed a new model of artificial intelligence governance inspired by the teachings of Pope Leo XIV as set out in his encyclical Magnifica Humanitas. The new model is intended to ensure that AI technologies are developed and used safely, fairly and with full respect for human rights.

items.story: A signal that appears to show ions moving inside a battery may, in fact, be an illusion caused by an uneven surface. A KAIST research team has identified the origin of this type of artifact, which can lead researchers to misinterpret what is happening inside a battery, and has developed a method to reduce it.

items.headline: War drama Pressure depicts D‑day's weather forecast—what we found when we recreated the challenge using modern systems
items.teaser: Meteorologist James Stagg gave what many regard as the most important weather forecast in history in June 1944. The fate of more than 150…
items.story: Meteorologist James Stagg gave what many regard as the most important weather forecast in history in June 1944. The fate of more than 150,000 Allied troops preparing to invade the Normandy beaches on D-Day and the future of the war in Europe depended on Stagg and his forecasting teams. Get the forecast wrong and an already perilous invasion might not succeed, prolonging the war. In the briefing room at Southwick House near Portsmouth, waiting for the forecast, sat General Dwight D. Eisenhower.

items.headline: Deep biosphere has endured mountain-building and erosion over hundreds of millions of years
items.teaser: A new study reveals that microbial life deep within Earth has persisted and repeatedly flourished through hundreds of millions of years o…
items.story: A new study reveals that microbial life deep within Earth has persisted and repeatedly flourished through hundreds of millions of years of mountain-building and erosion. By analyzing minerals, fluids and gases from a 2.3-kilometer-deep (1.4-mile-deep) borehole in central Sweden, researchers have uncovered episodic bursts of methane-producing life linked to major geological events that shaped Scandinavia. The paper is published in the journal Communications Earth & Environment.

items.headline: Indonesia’s most dangerous fires are burning underground
items.teaser: Indonesia’s dangerous peat fires are surging early in the 2026 fire season as a strengthening El Niño and severe drought dry out wetlands…
items.story: Indonesia’s dangerous peat fires are surging early in the 2026 fire season as a strengthening El Niño and severe drought dry out wetlands that can burn underground for months. These slow smoldering fires are especially destructive because they release far more fine particles and several pollutants than typical tropical forest fires, while thick smoke can make them difficult for satellites to detect.

In one experiment, it predicted a damaging instability about 200 milliseconds before it appeared and adjusted the plasma to stop it from forming.

items.headline: Scientists find a weak spot in one of the deadliest brain cancers
items.teaser: Researchers may have found a new way to weaken glioblastoma’s defenses against treatment. Blocking a protein called SET prevented tumors …
items.story: Researchers may have found a new way to weaken glioblastoma’s defenses against treatment. Blocking a protein called SET prevented tumors from forming in preclinical models, while targeting related proteins made cancer cells more vulnerable to radiation. The strategy works by restoring activity of PP2A, an enzyme that glioblastoma cells appear to suppress. Human testing will be needed to determine whether the approach is safe and effective.

items.story: Scientists used Earth’s magnetic field and atmosphere as a planet-sized detector to search for some of the lightest proposed forms of dark matter. The approach dramatically improved limits on ultralight axions and uncovered several intriguing dark photon signals that still need to be explained.

items.headline: 80,000-year-old “arrowheads” rewrite human history
items.teaser: Archaeologists have identified tiny 80,000-year-old projectile points in Uzbekistan that may have been used like arrowheads. Their size, …
items.story: Archaeologists have identified tiny 80,000-year-old projectile points in Uzbekistan that may have been used like arrowheads. Their size, design, and impact damage closely resemble weapons found much later at a Homo sapiens site in France. The discovery suggests sophisticated projectile technology may have appeared in Central Asia long before modern humans became firmly established in Europe, potentially rewriting a major chapter of human migration.

items.headline: Life uses 4 DNA letters. Scientists just made 8 work
items.teaser: Researchers at UC San Diego have demonstrated that a key cellular enzyme can accurately read an eight-letter genetic alphabet, doubling t…
items.story: Researchers at UC San Diego have demonstrated that a key cellular enzyme can accurately read an eight-letter genetic alphabet, doubling the four letters used by all known life on Earth. Detailed imaging revealed that RNA polymerase handles synthetic DNA letters in surprisingly similar ways to natural ones. The finding brings scientists closer to building expanded genetic systems that could perform entirely new biological functions.
